magic-valley-residents-unidentified-elon.headline: Magic Valley Residents - Unidentified Elongated Object Over Buhl Nov 4
magic-valley-residents-unidentified-elon.author: Dakota Frandsen
magic-valley-residents-unidentified-elon.core: Posted in last 7 days Magic Valley Residents - Unidentified Elongated Object Over Buhl Nov 4 On the evening of November 4, between approximately 7:15 and 7:30 PM, something crossed the sky over Buhl, Idaho, and we're looking for other witnesses. A large dark, elongated object was observed nearly overhead, moving from the south-southwest toward the north-northwest for roughly a minute before fading slowly from view in an open, dark sky. Two additional lights were also seen, which the primary witness reported as appearing to respond to the main object. No sound was reported. At least one common explanation was ruled out in real time. A satellite-tracker check confirmed no Starlink overhead. Other conventional explanations remain under review. Reported by Dakota Frandsen of the Bald and Bonkers Network and the FrandsenFiles archive, who observed and documented the event in real time, including a live satellite-tracker check to rule out Starlink. Please report only what you actually saw, in your own words, before reading further details, matching details alone are not treated as confirmation. If you were in the Buhl, Twin Falls, or greater Magic Valley area that evening and saw anything unusual in the sky, even briefly, we'd like to hear from you. Times, directions, durations, photos, or even "I saw something but didn't think much of it" all help build a fuller picture. If you submit an account, photo, or video, please include the date, time, location, and direction you were facing. Reports may be quoted or referenced in published case materials; your contact information is optional and will not be published without your permission. Submitting does not create any confidential relationship, and we may follow up with questions. This is an open, reported event under investigation. If our assessment changes as evidence comes in, we will update and correct this notice publicly. You can reply here or reach us directly at [email redacted]. #Buhl #Idaho #MagicValley #skywatch #frandsenfiles Bald and Bonkers Network

seed-to-early-series-a-b2b-founders-foun.headline: Seed to Early Series A B2B Founders - Founder-Led Sales Handoff
seed-to-early-series-a-b2b-founders-foun.author: Erika Sestok
seed-to-early-series-a-b2b-founders-foun.core: Posted in last 7 days Seed to Early Series A B2B Founders - Founder-Led Sales Handoff Sachin Kansal at Uber has a rule about "dogfooding": you do not get to fix the product until you sit in the customer's seat and feel the friction yourself. Before I scale groundwork., I am applying that exact rule to my own business. Most B2B founders I talk to are trapped in the same loop. The product works. Customers are signing. But every deal still runs through them. They know it cannot stay that way. What is less clear is how to hand it off without watching pipeline stall out. That stretch is my zone of genuis. I ran sales and account management teams at Uber Eats, then built GTM at startups where none of it existed yet. But I do not want to build groundwork. on assumptions about your business. So I am running an interview series called The Handoff. I am sitting down with B2B founders to dig into what it actually takes to move past founder-led sales. What you tried, what you paid for, what stuck, and what did not. Here is what to expect: • A 25-minute Zoom where I ask questions and you talk. • No pitch. I am not there to diagnose your business or hand you an unsolicited roadmap. If you want my take, ask and you will get it. • Private notes. I record only so I can listen instead of typing. The recording stays with me. • Your call. Nothing gets shared without your OK, named or anonymous. • The Handoff Report. When the series wraps, you get the full breakdown of what every founder tried, what it cost, what worked, and what the ones who made it through did differently. Most founders figure this out in a silo. The report is a chance to see how your peers are navigating the exact same ceiling. I am looking to speak with: • B2B founders (seed to early Series A) still closing most deals themselves • Founders whose first sales hire did not go the way they hoped • Founders who successfully made the transition and can share how If that is you, drop a comment or send me a DM. If someone comes to mind, I would love the intro.

diwali-celebrants-small-rituals-of-love.headline: Diwali Celebrants - Small Rituals Of Love
diwali-celebrants-small-rituals-of-love.author: Vijay Sharma
diwali-celebrants-small-rituals-of-love.core: Posted in last 7 days Diwali Celebrants - Small Rituals Of Love Your Diwali Ritual of Love In two days, the lamps will be lit. Millions of them, on doorsteps, rooftops, windowsills and walls. And behind every single one, there is a small story of love. We speak of Diwali as a festival of lights. But when I think back across the years, it is not the lights I remember most. It is the hands that lit them. The rituals of the people who made the house ready. The grandmother who insisted the first lamp be placed at the doorstep, for whoever might be coming home. The father who climbed the roof every year to hang the same old string of lights, muttering at the tangles, refusing all help. The mother who made sweets for the neighbours before she made them for her own family. The child who was finally trusted to light one diya by herself, and held the matchstick as if it were made of gold. These are not grand traditions. They are small, repeated acts of love, made holy by returning to them, year after year. Just like the evening lamp we spoke of last week. So today, the Reader’s Chair is yours again. Tell me about your Diwali ritual of love. Not the shopping, not the decorations, but the one small thing your family does, or did, that holds the whole festival together for you. A lamp placed in a certain spot. A sweet made only once a year. A prayer said at a particular moment. A person who is no longer with you, but whose ritual you still keep. And if Diwali is not your festival, tell me about the light you keep in your own tradition. Love has many festivals, and every one of them has its lamps. Write it in the comments below, or send it to me privately at [email redacted], in any language your heart speaks. On Sunday, Diwali day, I will share a few of your rituals, without names unless you wish, in my Diwali essay, The Lamp That Came. Let us light this Diwali together, one story at a time. Four lines for you and me today : Not crackers’ roar, not shining gold, but hands that keep what hands once told; one lamp, one sweet, one prayer, one door: the ritual love returns us for. Tell yourself : Which small Diwali ritual of love would you never let go of? Love : Kindness : Compassion : Gratitude Thank you for spending these moments with me. — Vijay Sharma SHIVAM – An Art Studio · Goa · Pune Books: https://lnkd.in/dnX2R2Sq You Came: coming 31 December 2026. Follow the road to it in 75 Days to You Came. Write to me: [email redacted]

early-career-workers-future-of-work-and-.core: Posted in last 7 days Early Career Workers - Future of Work & AI Are you at the start of your working life? We'd love to hear from you. At The Future Collective, we're working with Henley Business School on a new report into the future of work. Most of the debate asks what AI will do to work. We're asking a different question: how should work change because AI exists, and what would it take to get there? To answer that properly, we need to hear from people who are starting out right now. We'd love to speak to: 01 Graduates: finished university and looking for a first role 02 Apprentices: on an apprenticeship, or newly qualified from college 03 Straight to work: in an entry-level job after leaving school or college 04 Outside work: not in work, education or training right now 05 Insecure work: temporary, gig, zero-hours, or working below your qualifications It's a relaxed, confidential conversation online, lasting around an hour. There's no need to prepare and there are no right or wrong answers. We just want to hear about your own experiences of work so far, and what you think needs to change. We're holding interviews over the next few weeks. If this sounds like you, or someone you know, please send me a message. Sharing this post would really help us reach the voices that are too often missing from conversations about the future of work. #FutureOfWork #EarlyCareers #Careers #AI

cisos-and-senior-cybersecurity-leaders-p.headline: CISOs & Senior Cybersecurity Leaders - Protecting Developers
cisos-and-senior-cybersecurity-leaders-p.author: Edward Targett
cisos-and-senior-cybersecurity-leaders-p.core: Posted in last 7 days CISOs & Senior Cybersecurity Leaders - Protecting Developers The world's largest heist, the hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance, started when a developer there downloaded malware whilst trying to install "a popular AI coding tool." (They were later tricked into taking a fake job interview and doing a coding "test" that led them to download more malware.) The recent compromise of an important code repository belonging to European cloud provider OVHcloud also started because a developer unwittingly downloaded a malicious software extension onto their personal MacBook, so they could use funky colours on their laptop. (Visual Studio Code extension Colour Picker Universal version 2.8.91, since you asked.) Developers are also being targeted further “upstream”; overwhelmed open-source project operators have been groomed into accepting help on their projects; help that turns out to be malicious and designed to compromise software supply chains at staggering scale. (xz-utils still reverberates.) I’d like to write a deep-dive for The Stack into how security functions are thinking about how they protect their developers; across everything from security awareness and training, via #BYOC policy guardrails, #EDR, and beyond. I’m particularly interested in hearing from #CISOs and other senior #cybersecurity figures about this. If you’d like to share your views (or #PR friends, you think you have a client spokesperson who might be strong and experience on this; please no generic AI fluff) do pop me an email with “protecting developers” in the subject line. #infosec #journorequest #techpr The Stack

lighting-industry-associations-podcast-s.core: Posted in last 7 days Lighting Industry Associations - Podcast Season 2 Guests From a building site to a podcast studio… and somehow we've made it to the end of Season 1! 🎙️ The Built by People Season 1 finale is officially LIVE! When team DFL-UK started this podcast back in March, the idea was simple. Get people talking, share experiences and have some honest conversations about the people behind our industry. And what a journey it's been! We've had some brilliant guests, interesting conversations and plenty of laughs along the way. For our final episode, Ryan Carroll and I are doing things a little differently. We're taking you behind the scenes of DFL, looking at how our office refurbishment came together, how we created our podcast studio and reflecting on what we've learnt from our first season. And yes, Ryan and I probably spend a fair bit of time winding each other up too! What I've enjoyed most is hearing different perspectives and being reminded that our industry is full of interesting people with stories worth sharing. A massive thank you to everyone who's joined us, watched, listened or supported the podcast. James Probut Jack Edward Mersh Bradley Russell Connor MacDonald Amelia Bateman-Wood Piers Lowbridge Rebecca Hatch MBA IEng FILP Paul Murphy Rebecca Fletcher And SO many more from the Institution of Lighting Professionals Annual summit in Birmingham! But we're not finished yet! We're already thinking about Season 2, and I'd love to hear from you. especially the Highway Electrical Association (HEA) The Lighting Industry Association (The LIA) SLL - Society of Light and Lighting and Women Lighting Professionals (WLP) Would you fancy joining us as a guest?
